# Checks the gates don't run yet, each with what in a tree needs it and the piece before which it must go live. A tree
# that needs one bounces until the coordinator's ref that adds the check removes its line. Triggers: file:<path> (a
# file or folder under the workspace), text:<regex> (the fork's C, comments left out, matching it), and table:<name> (a
# table beside this file with any line). The queue holds the include-tree check's trigger itself, since it depends on
# files outside the workspace.
# check

a check that `CREATE DATABASE` copies each storage of the template into the new repository as section 5 moves one, with no fold (the newest base's chunks copied whole, every version the base doesn't apply carried with its writer, each copy logged as a built base, from the template's states and manifest alone), and copies the template's database-level trees, which belong to no storage (item 10's identity tree, its manifest tree and delta versions; the table data tree's parts come with that tree, Order 3), the carried versions and the trees' versions counted at their writers' entries as a rewrite's carried versions are, so it reads no catalog of the template and opens no writer in it, with its cases: a template with unfolded rows, including a table keyed by a compared column, gives a new database those rows in order and leaves the template unchanged; a table made in the template reads in the new database with the template's object id, and a write to it records no new pair; and a standby replays the copy to the same rows (design item 6; MacPF 14, 2026-11-16)

a check that ALTER DATABASE SET TABLESPACE first makes the database's storages usable, re-keys each storage under the new tablespace by the same per-storage copy as CREATE DATABASE's, with no fold, and keys their states under the new tablespace, so no state keeps the old directory as its own and every checkpoint after the move saves them (the move text's section 5), with a case: a database with delta rows, including a table keyed by a compared column, moved, a checkpoint, a restart, the rows read in order

a check that `AddEnumLabel`'s renumber of an enum's sort orders (`RenumberEnumType`) rewrites every relation whose keys hold the type (`type_contains`), as Doltgrust's `rewrite_tables_keyed_by_enum` does, with its case (design item 4's enum keys)
column3: the table access method's first stored key

column1: a fold that fails (item 8's "A fold that fails"; design A leaves no refused install): a storage whose fold raises reports it, backs off, and its database's other storages still fold, with its cases: a standby whose comparator table's fold always raises while replay passes delta_memory, and replay goes on; and delta_memory filled while a long snapshot holds the fold's point back, and writers go on

the unknown methods' text's validate scan's unique check: a concurrent build's validation of a unique btree index the fork stores refuses a row whose key another live row holds with the reference's 23505, since only btree has amcanunique and its unique check is the btree's part 2 (orev-16's R2)

bugs rows 125, 142, and 156's rule: every walk of a storage's delta versions (a reader's under every snapshot kind, the fold's folded_rows, the recount's, and redo's) drops the versions its base folded through one accessor, with row 125's SnapshotAny case and row 142's fold after a crash restart following an earlier fold, each counting a keyless table's rows once, and row 156's scan held at an injection point mid-delta while a fold installs and drops, which returns every row

bugs row 104's rule, the tables' part: the fork's VACUUM sets relfrozenxid to the oldest xid (sub or top) a table's and its fork indexes' delta versions name, rows, free space, and value maps alike, at most the cutoffs' OldestXmin, and relminmxid to the next multixact, so datfrozenxid and commit log truncation never pass a live version's writer, with its cases: a VACUUM FREEZE held at an unfolded writer, moved on after a fold, and held at an unfolded fork index entry's writer

bugs row 104's rule, the identity tree's part: every writer of item 10's identity tree versions keeps a live entry in the fork's commit status table, its versions counted at their writers' entries until the save that drops them gives the counts back, and commit log truncation's bound (vac_truncate_clog's frozen xid lowered to the oldest top-level xid with a live entry) keeps those writers' commit log, since the tree belongs to no pg_class row, with its case: an identity tree version's writer whose commit log page truncation keeps (with item 10's identity tree, MacPF's origin/daylon/truncate-bound; the table data tree's part comes with that tree, Order 3)
column3: item 10's identity tree with the truncation bound (whichever of item10-ids and row 104 lands second)

column1: VACUUM's own fold (item 2's Freeing): a VACUUM of a fork table, autovacuum's included, folds the table and its indexes' storages at their own horizon-bounded point before its free, so a committed delete's tuple id comes back to the free space map at that VACUUM as heap's does, with its cases: 052's fed cases (73 to 77) run without the test's fold, and a plain DELETE then VACUUM giving the next insert the freed tuple id as heap's twin

item 10's table data tree's obligations, when that tree lands (Order 3): each checkpoint's save folds its committed versions into the manifest's tree and drops the superseded ones from the delta and the runs, giving their counts back, so it stays bounded however many tables are made and dropped, temporary ones included, with its case (many tables created and dropped across checkpoints, the tree's versions bounded, live layouts reading back after a restart); its writers keep live commit status entries under the commit log truncation bound, with its case (a table data tree version's writer whose commit log page truncation keeps); and CREATE DATABASE copies its parts, with its case (a table made in the template reads in the new database with its layout)

bugs row 168's rule: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY and REINDEX CONCURRENTLY of a fork btree build the index the reference builds: the validate scan takes its set from the index's own entries, not ambulkdelete's callback, so no row is inserted twice, and a unique concurrent build's validation refuses a row whose key another live row holds with the reference's 23505, with its cases: a keyless table's concurrent build counting each row once, a unique concurrent build refusing a concurrent duplicate, and REINDEX CONCURRENTLY of a fork btree equal to a plain REINDEX
047's cases rerun through real CLUSTER and VACUUM FULL, with the fork's routine every stored table's own, in place of doltgres_test_rewrite's stand-in (the rewrite text's section 4)

a check that the reader takes a delta version's epoch as the later of its commit and command's and its storage's base epoch when it was made, with a case of a rewrite's carried, re-formed version read after a later ADD COLUMN (PLAN's base record field 4)

047's standby conflict reads rerun as real SQL parallel seq scans (parallel_setup_cost 0, parallel_tuple_cost 0, min_parallel_table_scan_size 0, max_parallel_workers_per_gather 2, EXPLAIN showing a Parallel Seq Scan): 40001 on the standby's older snapshot, and every row on the primary's older snapshot and the standby's newer one (PRevPF 8's G5)

047's ALTER INDEX SET TABLESPACE case read through the fork index's scans, an index scan and an index-only scan of each moved index equal to its heap twin's, on the primary and on a restored, promoted server (the rewrite text's section 5, PRevPF 8's X1)

053's case of bugs row 107: a point-in-time recovery at delta_memory 1 MB whose replayed range writes more than delta_memory, with one transaction open across all of it, finishes, its open transaction's rows unseen and every committed row read back, once the startup's fold frees the budget's blocks in recovery (the budget wait text, draft 2)

fsck's I19 check reports a standby's tree in a comparator's order whose root differs from its primary's (PLAN item 8's "Standbys' roots"), with its case: 062's comparator mismatch, which the standby warns of and keeps its own root, reported by fsck

062's cold-standby case and row 107's point-in-time recovery case: a standby without hot standby whose startup process folds a byte-ordered tree at its replayed record's point and finds another root ends recovery with the hot standby's FATAL, and a point-in-time recovery replaying more than delta_memory with no fold worker finishes, its startup process folding each byte-ordered tree and never a comparator's, the startup's fold deciding outcomes by logged_outcome where xids aren't answered
062's case 38: a standby's read during the startup's in-order fold of past_budget (30 batches of 100 rows past delta_memory 8MB) returns every row, its count 3000
column3: row 156 (TxnPF's): 062's case 38, a standby's read during the startup's in-order fold

column1: a test that runs every ALTER TABLE subcommand over a fork table and compares the fork's layout with the catalog's columns (design item 10's layout; row 88's transforms)
column3: item 10's slice 2, the table data tree

column1: a case of EXPLAIN over a table with a fork btree index, and again after TRUNCATE gives it a new relfilenode, planning with no read of the index's file, since the fork's amgettreeheight answers from its base (CommPF 9's ruling (a))
column3: the switch or the btree's part 2, slice 6, whichever lands second

column1: a serializable scan of a fork btree takes its SIREAD targets on the leaf pages the fold numbers (item 7), and aminsert checks them, with the cross-fold case (CommPF 9's rulings, 2026-11-16; an index-only scan of a fork btree fetches each row, which takes its predicate lock as any fetch does, bugs row 190)
column3: the fork indexes' leaf page locks (item 7)

column1: a parallel index scan and a parallel index-only scan of a fork btree run by Postgres' parallel workers under Gather Merge give heap's twin's rows in order (the btree's part 2, §4), the workers getting the fork's routine through the relcache's call site
column3: the switch or the btree's part 2, slice 6, whichever lands second

column1: 028's key orders through the real commands: for each type 028 checks that a primary key may have, a fork table keyed by it, filled by INSERT, whose seq scan gives its rows in the reference's ORDER BY order, where 028 checks the keys through doltgres_test_key over heap tables (the switch's coverage of the pre-switch suites, which keep their tables heap through doltgres_test_twins)

033's scan cases through the real commands: a fork table's rows written by INSERT and folded into its base, read by SELECT through seq scans, index fetches, cursors, and rescans, against the reference's output, where 033 drives them through doltgres_test_base and doltgres_test_scan over heap tables (the switch's coverage of the pre-switch suites, which keep their tables heap through doltgres_test_twins)

034's comparator cases through the real commands: fork tables keyed by each type 034 keys by a comparison function, filled by INSERT, read by seq scan in key order and fetched by ctid against the reference's ORDER BY output, with the nested read of a comparison function that reads a fork table (the switch's coverage of the pre-switch suites, which keep their tables heap through doltgres_test_twins)

035's TID range cases through the real commands: SELECT with ctid range quals over a fork table filled by INSERT, within a block, across blocks, and past the end, against the reference's rows (the switch's coverage of the pre-switch suites, which keep their tables heap through doltgres_test_twins)

036's parallel scan cases through the real commands: a fork table's parallel seq scan gives the serial scan's rows over a base and a delta, and a session whose snapshot predates a fold reads the versions the fold kept for it (the switch's coverage of the pre-switch suites, which keep their tables heap through doltgres_test_twins)

038's insert cases through the real commands: INSERT, COPY's multi_insert, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT's speculative inserts, toasted and overflowed values, and logical decoding of a user_catalog_table's inserts on fork tables, with the ctids and decoded changes 038 checks through doltgres_test_insert over heap tables, against heap twins' and the reference's (the switch's coverage of the pre-switch suites, which keep their tables heap through doltgres_test_twins)

042's snapshot cases through the real commands: a fork table's rows read under a REPEATABLE READ snapshot that predates a running writer's insert and a committed delete, and the dirty and NonVacuumable reads Postgres makes of it (a unique check's and VACUUM's), against the reference's (the switch's coverage of the pre-switch suites, which keep their tables heap through doltgres_test_twins)

045's btree cases through the real commands: CREATE INDEX on fork tables and its base, inserts through aminsert, VACUUM's bulk delete and cleanup counts, and an index delta's fold, which 045 drives through doltgres_test_index_build, doltgres_test_index_base, and doltgres_test_vacuum over heap tables (the switch's coverage of the pre-switch suites, which keep their tables heap through doltgres_test_twins)

046's delete, update, and row lock cases through the real commands: DELETE, UPDATE, SELECT FOR UPDATE, FOR SHARE, and FOR KEY SHARE on fork tables, with their concurrent sessions' waits and serialization failures, and the ctids and latest tids 046 checks through doltgres_test_write over heap tables, against heap twins' (the switch's coverage of the pre-switch suites, which keep their tables heap through doltgres_test_twins)

047's storage swap cases other than its CLUSTER and VACUUM FULL line's through the real commands: TRUNCATE in place and by a new relfilenode, ALTER TABLE rewrites, and their crash and standby replays on fork tables, which 047 drives through doltgres_test_new_file, doltgres_test_truncate, and doltgres_test_rewrite over heap tables (the switch's coverage of the pre-switch suites, which keep their tables heap through doltgres_test_twins)

050's fold cases through the real commands: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and COMMIT PREPARED on fork tables, each commit's end at its entry and the versions it counts, folded and read back by SELECT, which 050 checks through doltgres_test_insert and doltgres_test_fold over heap tables (the switch's coverage of the pre-switch suites, which keep their tables heap through doltgres_test_twins)

052's VACUUM cases through the real commands: VACUUM and autovacuum of fork tables freeing tuple ids that later INSERTs take again, with the ctids heap gives on the reference (Differences rows 43 and 47), and a standby following them, which 052 checks through doltgres_test_vacuum and doltgres_test_write over heap tables, against heap twins' (the switch's coverage of the pre-switch suites, which keep their tables heap through doltgres_test_twins)

061's cases other than its CONCURRENTLY line's through the real commands: hash, GiST, and exclusion-constrained indexes on fork tables, read by index and bitmap scans after writes and a VACUUM, and their validation's merge, which 061 drives through doltgres_test_index_validate and doltgres_test_write over heap tables, against heap twins' (the switch's coverage of the pre-switch suites, which keep their tables heap through doltgres_test_twins)

037's size cases through the real commands: pg_relation_size, the planner's page and tuple estimates, and ANALYZE's counts of fork tables filled by INSERT, against heap twins' pages for the same rows, where 037 saves bases through doltgres_test_base over heap tables (the switch's coverage of the pre-switch suites, which keep their tables heap through doltgres_test_twins)

fsck's I19 check reports an entry of an index that keeps records (an expression or partial index, CommPF 10's no-user-code removal) with no record of its row, and a record that names no entry, with its case: a record-keeping index whose record a test removes alone, reported by fsck

the merge reaches an index that keeps records only through its entries' records (CommPF 10's no-user-code removal): a merged row change removes ours' old entry with the record that names it, running no index expression, and writes the merged row's entry with its record, with its case: two branches each update a row of an expression-indexed table, the merge holds one entry and one record per row, and a DELETE of a merged row evaluates no expression
